children: By Panarat Thepgumpanat and Chayut Setboonsarng

Sugar production in Thailand, the world's second-largest exporter of the commodity after Brazil, is expected to fall 12.5% to 10.5 million metric tons in the 2026/27 season, an industry official said.
The forecast drop is a result of drought, higher input costs and farmers switching to cassava, said Thawat Hamarn, director of strategy and planning at the Office of the Cane and Sugar Board.

Sugarcane output is expected to decline 9.5% to about 95 million tons from 105 million tons last season, according to Thawat, referring to the 2026/27 harvest that is expected to run from December through April.

Farmers have faced higher fertiliser costs, and cane prices have not been attractive enough, prompting some growers to switch to more profitable crops, said Naradhip Anantasuk, manager of the Thai Sugarcane Planters Federation.
Global sugar prices have risen amid expectations that drought could reduce production in Thailand, India and Brazil, according to Naradhip.
But prices would need to reach around 21 to 22 cents per pound for farmers to cover their costs, Naradhip said, compared to current prices of around 18 to 19 cents.

In Khon Kaen, a province in northeastern Thailand, about 450 kilometres (280 miles) from Bangkok, cane production could fall to 1.8 million tons, a local official said, compared to 5.86 million tons last season.
"Inconsistent rainfall, farmers' debt burdens and disease outbreaks would lead to lower cane production," said Chairat Kittivarapol, an official with a sugarcane growers' association in the province.
